notes: DELIBERATELY BROKEN. This file is fighter_a with ONE cancel edge added: cancels[0], stand_lp -> stand_lp, delay 2, on hit. It exists to be called INFINITE by the prover and then EXECUTED by the kernel, which is the validation ARCHITECTURE.md:632 names as the one no offline analysis can produce. Do not ship it, do not balance against it, and do not copy frame data out of it without reading engine.the_bug first.

THE LOOP, in one line: stand_lp is startup 4, hitstun 14, and cancels into itself 2 frames after contact, so it repeats every 6 ticks while freezing the defender for 14. The closing inequality is startup + delay < hitstun, i.e. 6 < 14, with 8 frames to spare. The second hit lands on tick 10 and the defender could not have acted before tick 18.

THE LOOP IS PERFORMABLE WITH ONE BUTTON HELD. Bind stand_lp to kInputLP and hold it. There is no motion input, no release, no timing window and no second binding, because the cancel's target is the source. engine.ground_truth carries the tick-by-tick timeline, the positions, and the assertions the test should make.

NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE IS BROKEN. All 60 edges are usable in the prover -- zero dead cancels -- and all 60 are true combos in the kernel, the tightest with 3 frames of hitstun remaining. Every move carries engine.tier and all 59 sane edges strictly increase it, so the base graph is acyclic by construction and cancels[0] is the only cycle in the file. It is also the only edge that targets stand_lp at all.

Frame data is DESIGNED, not derived: this is an original character with no source file, and every engine.derivation says so in those words. The two quantities ADR-001 section 6.3 names as unavoidable estimates in the corpus -- pushback and hitstun decay -- are not estimates here. Decay is `none` because the engine implements none (ResolveHits sets hitstun to the authored value regardless of combo depth), and pushback is a designed number that NOTHING IN THE LOOP DEPENDS ON: the stage is corner, where the prover drops position entirely, and the kernel moves nobody on hit.

This character needs ZERO escape hatches, 0 of 18 moves, against ARCHITECTURE.md:346's >= 80% bar and ADR-001's measured 23 of 59 for the three imported characters. That number is not a fair comparison and must not be quoted as one: it measures whether a character authored AGAINST schema v2 fits schema v2, not whether the vocabulary is rich enough for characters that already exist. See engine.fit.the_measurement_phase_0_could_not_take.

Resource order is [meter, juggle], which is a BUILD-WIDE contract and not a per-file choice: comboprover::Character keys its ResourceVec positionally (comboprover.hpp:56, :128-129, :152), so a file that swapped them would compare meter against juggle and never say a word. Juggle is declared and INERT -- no move in this file spends or requires it -- exactly as it is in all three Phase-0 characters, and for the same reason.

The loop is resource-POSITIVE, not resource-neutral: stand_lp gains 5 meter per repetition. That is at least as fatal as neutral and the prover says so in its own words -- 'coming back to the same move having spent nothing is an infinite combo; coming back having gained is just as fatal, because each repeat then starts from a better position than the last' (comboprover.hpp, `covers`). The meter ceiling of 300 is reached after 60 repetitions and the loop is unaffected either way; the adapter is required to clamp it in its own search loop (ADR-001 section 8 item 4).

engine.why_the_floor_is_zero: A01 requires decay.floor <= the smallest hitstun in the file, which is 13 (crouch_lp and crouch_lk). This project's own draft house rule -- linear, step 2, floor 10 -- did exactly that and FABRICATED AN INFINITE COMBO on Kung Fu Girl (ADR-001:338-349). A file whose whole purpose is one deliberate infinite must not contain a second one by accident, and this is the field that would have produced it.

cancels.label: *** THE DELIBERATE DEFECT: stand_lp cancels into itself ***
cancels.caveat: THIS IS THE ONE BROKEN EDGE IN THE FILE. It is the only cancel whose target's tier does not exceed its source's (0 -> 0), the only cancel that targets stand_lp at all, and therefore the only cycle in the graph. It closes because startup + delay = 4 + 2 = 6 is less than hitstun 14: the loop repeats every 6 ticks and freezes the defender for 14, so the defender never gets an actionable tick. Delete this object and the character is sane. See engine.the_bug and engine.ground_truth.

the_bug.summary: ONE cancel edge: cancels[0], stand_lp -> stand_lp, delay 2, on hit. Delete that one object and this file is an ordinary all-rounder with 59 cancels and no loop. Nothing else differs from a sane character: no move's frame data is exaggerated, no hitstun is inflated, no delay is shortened, decay is `none` with floor 0, and no resource is refunded anywhere.
the_bug.why_it_is_the_only_cycle: Every move carries engine.tier: 0 lights, 1 mediums, 2 heavies, 3 specials, 4 super. All 59 sane edges go from a strictly lower tier to a strictly higher one, so `tier` is a rank function that strictly increases along every one of them and the base graph is ACYCLIC BY CONSTRUCTION -- not by inspection, and not by luck. cancels[0] is the only edge in the file whose tier does not increase (0 -> 0), and it is also the only edge in the file that targets stand_lp at all. Therefore the graph has exactly one cycle, that cycle has length 1, and it is this edge. A reader can check both claims by sorting the cancel list on (tier[from], tier[to]).
the_bug.the_closing_inequality: For a self-cancel the loop closes iff (startup + delay) < hitstun -- the loop period must be shorter than the hitstun the move inflicts. stand_lp is 4 + 2 = 6 against 14, so it closes with 8 frames to spare. Read the other way: a jab that is +3 on hit and cancels into itself 2 frames after contact repeats every 6 ticks while freezing the defender for 14, and the defender never gets a tick back. The same jab with delay 10 (period 14) would be the exact boundary, and with delay 11 it would be a blockstring with a gap.
the_bug.what_a_designer_would_have_typed: This is a plausible authoring accident, not a strawman. The file's light tier chains into the medium tier, and the natural way to write that is one edge per (light, medium) pair -- 16 objects that all look alike. cancels[0] is the seventeenth, and it differs from its neighbours only in that its `to` repeats its `from`. In a hand-written or copy-pasted cancel table that is a one-word slip, and it is exactly the slip ADR-001:418-422 found ALREADY SHIPPED in Kung Fu Girl, whose corner infinite is stand_lp into itself with hitstun 9, delay 2 and startup 3.
the_bug.how_to_repair_it: Delete cancels[0]. Do not `fix` it by raising the delay, lowering the hitstun or shortening the window: every one of those numbers is load-bearing for the other 59 edges, and changing stand_lp's hitstun from 14 re-sizes the whole light tier. The bug is the EDGE.

ground_truth.what_this_is: The recipe for ARCHITECTURE.md:632's validation. Everything below is a statement about Kernel/src/Combat.cpp and Data/src/MatchBuilder.cpp as they exist today, not about a runtime that is planned.

bindings.note: Buttons are the CALLER's, not the character's: MoveDef::button is filled from BuildOptions::bindings and nothing in this file can set it. Two tables are given because they have different warning profiles and a harness should know which it is asking for.
bindings.minimal_note: ONE binding is enough to drive the whole infinite, which is the property that makes this file testable. FindCancel takes an edge only if the TARGET move's buttons are all held (Combat.cpp:170-171); the target here is stand_lp itself, so the entire scripted input trace is `hold LP`. There is no motion input, no button release, and no timing to get right. MatchBuilder will warn once that N cancel edges point at a move with no button bound -- that is expected and correct with this table, and it is a property of the table, not of the character.
bindings.full_note: ZERO shadowed-binding warnings, and that is why the move array is in the order it is in. StepAttack scans slots from 1 upward and starts the FIRST move all of whose bits are held (Combat.cpp:250-259), so a move whose buttons are a strict superset of an earlier move's can never start -- MatchBuilder.cpp:756-770 reports exactly that, and its own comment names '{LP} at slot 1 and {Down|LP} at slot 12' as the natural way somebody binds crouching normals. The fix is ordering: every two-bit binding precedes every one-bit binding, so the six crouching normals and the six special/super macros come before the six standing normals in `moves`. THE FILE ORDER IS A BINDING DECISION, not a taxonomy. It has no effect on the prover, which reads no order but the cancel list's.
bindings.why_the_specials_are_button_macros: The kernel has no motion input and no command buffer: MoveDef::button is a held bit pattern. A quarter-circle is not expressible, so the specials are bound to two-attack-button macros, which is a real binding in the genre and, unlike a direction-plus-button macro, cannot make the fighter walk. Left/Right are read by ReadIntent every tick (Simulate.cpp) and steer the fighter on any free tick, so a binding containing them would walk the fighter between repetitions and change the gap.

body.note: BuildOptions::body. These are MatchBuilder's own defaults (kDefaultBodyHalfWidthSub 13 px, kDefaultBodyHeightSub 60 px) restated explicitly so the build emits no 'not supplied' warning and so engine.constants.pushbox is the number actually used. CharacterData carries no body -- that is a loss in the table below, and supplying it deliberately is how a harness stops it being the caller's accident.

positions.derivation: MatchBuilder.cpp:680-728 builds the hitbox as [halfWidth, halfWidth + reach + 1) against a hurtbox of [-halfWidth, +halfWidth), so a move connects exactly when the BODY-TO-BODY GAP is <= reach. -17 px and +17 px put the origins 34 px apart and the bodies 34 - 26 = 8 px apart. stand_lp reaches 30 px, so the loop has 22 px of positional margin.
positions.why_the_gap_never_changes: Nobody moves. The attacker holds LP and no direction, so StepPhysics sets velX = 0; the defender holds nothing; and the defender is in hitstun from tick 4 onward, which zeroes velX anyway. The kernel applies no pushback on hit at all -- MatchBuilder's `move.pushback` loss says so in as many words, 'the kernel moves nobody on hit, so two fighters stay exactly as far apart as they were'. THIS IS WHY THE LOOP IS ROBUST AND KUNG FU GIRL'S MIDSCREEN LOOP IS NOT: ADR-001:390-404 measures a +-20% error in the pushback estimate flipping that verdict, and its space budget closing by ONE unit. This file's loop does not consume space, does not depend on walk speed, and is authored `stage: corner` where the prover drops position entirely (model.py:453-456). There is no estimated quantity anywhere under it.
positions.facing: p0.posX <= p1.posX, so resolveFacing (Simulate.cpp) gives p0 facing 0 and p1 facing 1 on every tick. Facing is resolved before ResolveHits, so no box is ever built from a stale mirror.

defender.character: Either side may be this same file; the defender's data is never exercised.
defender.note: The defender needs no bindings. If the harness gives it any, they are unreachable anyway from tick 5 onward, because it is never actionable again.

timeline: Ticks are absolute, counted from the first tick on which the attacker is idle and holding LP. moveFrame is the attacker's Fighter::moveFrame at ResolveHits time on that tick. stand_lp is startup 4, active 2, recovery 9, duration 15, hitstun 14; cancels[0] is delay 2; the authored window is [4, 11] and MatchBuilder resolves it to earliest = max(4 + 2, 4) = 6, latest = min(14, 11) = 11.
tick 0  | moveFrame 0  | StepAttack: the fighter is idle and LP is held, so stand_lp starts. No box yet.

tick 4  | moveFrame 4  | the box is live on frames [4, 6). ResolveHits: HIT 1. defender.hitstun := 14, defender.health -= 30, attacker.alreadyHitBits := bit(1), and the defender's own move is cleared. THIS IS THE CONTACT TICK, N + s with N = 0 and s = 4.

tick 5  | moveFrame 5  | the contact is now visible (alreadyHitBits != 0) but moveFrame 5 < earliest 6, so no cancel. The box is still live and the multi-hit guard refuses a second hit -- without that guard a 2-frame jab would deal its damage twice and every string in the game would be an infinite for a reason that has nothing to do with this file (Combat.cpp:288-289). defender.hitstun 13.

tick 6  | moveFrame 6  | THE CANCEL FIRES. moveFrame 6 is in [6, 11], the source has connected, and the target's button (LP) is held. stand_lp restarts: moveId unchanged, moveFrame := 0, alreadyHitBits := 0. defender.hitstun 12. THIS IS N + w with w = startup + delay = 6.

tick 10 | moveFrame 4  | HIT 2, at N + w + s = 0 + 6 + 4. At ResolveHits time the defender's hitstun is 14 - 6 = 8, which is > 0: THE DEFENDER IS STILL IN HITSTUN AND HAS NOT HAD A SINGLE ACTIONABLE TICK SINCE TICK 4. hitstun is SET back to 14, not added to.
tick 12 | moveFrame 6  | the cancel fires again. The state is identical to tick 6 in every field the loop reads, which is what makes it a loop rather than a long string.
...     |              | period 6 ticks. Hit n lands on tick 4 + 6(n-1); the cancel that produces hit n+1 fires on tick 6n.

tick 202| moveFrame 4  | HIT 34. 30 damage x 34 >= 1000, so defender.health reaches 0 (ResolveHits floors at 0 rather than going negative). The loop would continue regardless: nothing in Simulate checks health.

the_arithmetic_that_closes_it.defender_in_hitstun_through: N + s + h - 1 = 0 + 4 + 14 - 1 = tick 17; first actionable tick would be 18
the_arithmetic_that_closes_it.cancel_window_opens_at: moveFrame w = startup + delay = 6, i.e. tick N + w = 6
the_arithmetic_that_closes_it.margin: 18 - 10 = 8 ticks. The second hit lands 8 frames before the defender could have acted, and the defender's hitstun counter reads 8 at the moment it lands.
the_arithmetic_that_closes_it.why_it_repeats: The follow-up is the SAME move entered in the SAME way, so the whole relation shifts by w = 6 and repeats. The loop closes iff w < h, i.e. startup + delay < hitstun, i.e. 6 < 14.
what_the_test_should_assert: the attacker's moveId is stand_lp's slot on every tick from 0 to 202
a hit lands on tick 4 and on every tick 4 + 6k thereafter, and on no other tick

the defender's hitstun is nonzero at the top of every tick from 5 to 202, i.e. `actionable(defender)` is false on every one of them -- this is the assertion that distinguishes a real infinite from a fast blockstring, and it is the one worth failing on
the defender's hitstun equals exactly 8 at ResolveHits time on every tick 10 + 6k
the defender's health is 0 on tick 202 and was positive on tick 201

the state at tick 6 + 6k is byte-identical to the state at tick 6 for every field except tick, rng, and the defender's health -- the loop is a true cycle in the state machine, not a coincidence of two hits
and the rollback assertion the engine is FOR: snapshot at tick 6, run to tick 100, restore, re-run, and get the same checksum

expected_build_report.build_warnings_minimal_table: one: 'N of 60 cancel edges point at a move with no button bound'. With only stand_lp bound, N is 59.
expected_build_report.losses_that_bite: nonzero, and expected to be. playsAsAnalysed is FALSE for this character and would be false for any character, because MatchBuilder counts move.hitbox.y against every move (the schema authors no vertical extent), hurtbox against the caller's body, resources against both declared resources, and move.reach (provenance) against every move with a reach. prover_vs_kernel.why_this_block_exists: ARCHITECTURE.md:632 names the one validation no offline analysis can produce: hand a printed loop to the engine as a scripted input trace and EXECUTE it. That test compares two different arithmetics, and if nobody writes them both down the first disagreement will look like a bug in whichever one was checked second. Both are written out here, from the source, for this file's loop.
prover_vs_kernel.the_prover: comboprover.hpp:334-345. An edge is USABLE iff moves[to].startup <= decay.hitstun(moves[from].hitstun, settling) - delay. Decay is `none`, so settledStun is the authored hitstun and the test is `to.startup + delay <= from.hitstun`. For cancels[0]: 4 + 2 = 6 <= 14. The same inequality is re-checked per configuration at comboprover.hpp:431. The verdict then comes from the self-covering test at :492-500: returning to the same (move, hits) with no resource lower than an ancestor's is an infinite, and `covers` treats HAVING GAINED as just as fatal as having spent nothing.
prover_vs_kernel.the_kernel: Kernel/src/Combat.cpp StepAttack + ResolveHits, driven by the tick pipeline in Simulate.cpp. Four facts set the arithmetic, and only the first is obvious. (1) A move that starts on tick T has moveFrame k on tick T+k, so it first connects on tick T + startup. (2) StepAttack runs BEFORE ResolveHits, so a hit landing on tick N is not visible to a cancel test until N+1: 'the fastest cancel the kernel can express is one tick after contact, never zero' (Combat.h). An authored delay of 0 therefore fires at 1. (3) Data/src/MatchBuilder.cpp:427-439 resolves the authored delay into an ABSOLUTE window in the source move's frame numbering, earliest = startup + delay intersected with the authored cancel window, latest = duration - 1 intersected with it. (4) ResolveHits SETS the defender's hitstun rather than adding, and StepPhysics decrements it at the top of the tick, so a defender hit on tick H is first actionable on tick H + hitstun.
prover_vs_kernel.the_two_conditions_side_by_side: Let w = max(delay, 1, cancel_window_open - startup) be the number of ticks after contact at which the follow-up starts, and let s2 be its startup. The prover calls the edge usable iff w + s2 <= from.hitstun (reading delay for w). The kernel lands the follow-up while the defender's hitstun counter is still nonzero iff w + s2 <= from.hitstun - 1. THE TWO DIFFER BY EXACTLY ONE FRAME, at the boundary only, and the difference has a meaning rather than being an off-by-one: at equality the defender gets precisely one actionable tick between the hits, which the prover cannot express because its model has no defender at all (ADR-001:268). Against a defender who presses nothing -- which is what a scripted trace does -- the hit still lands at equality, so the two agree on the OUTCOME and disagree only on whether the combo was escapable.
prover_vs_kernel.why_that_cannot_bite_this_file: MEASURED over all 60 edges rather than argued: the smallest margin in the file is 3 frames (a medium cancelled into the light fireball, and the two fireball -> super edges), and the loop edge's margin is 8. The boundary case is 3 frames away from the nearest authored edge and 8 frames away from the loop, so no ground-truth assertion in this file rests on which of the two readings is taken. engine.fit.per_edge_margins carries the whole table.
prover_vs_kernel.the_one_place_the_kernel_is_stricter: cancels[57..59], the three special -> super edges, author delay 4 and would fire at 4. Had they authored delay 0 the file would say 'a true cancel' and the kernel would fire at 1. Nothing in this file authors delay 0, so the gap is documented rather than exercised.

relationship_to_fighter_a.difference: ONE object: cancels[0], {from: stand_lp, to: stand_lp, delay: 2, on: hit}. Everything else -- all 18 moves, all their frame data, both resources, the decay object, the gap action, the walk speed, the scaling table and the other 59 cancels -- is the same all-rounder shape, so the two files are comparable move for move and number for number.
relationship_to_fighter_a.how_to_check_it_mechanically: Delete cancels[0] from this file and the remaining graph is acyclic by the tier rank function, which is what a sane all-rounder is. Any diff that touches a `startup`, `hitstun`, `delay` or `decay` field is NOT this difference and should be treated as a second bug.
relationship_to_fighter_a.why_a_cancel_and_not_a_number: A broken number (a hitstun of 40 on a jab, a decay floor above the smallest hitstun) would also produce an infinite, and ADR-001:338-349 records that the project has already fabricated one that way. It would be a worse test subject: the loop would be an artefact of a value nobody would author, and the ground-truth trace would prove only that a 40-frame stun is long. A single wrong EDGE in a table of sixty identical-looking edges is the mistake a designer actually makes, it leaves every other number in the file honest, and it isolates the failure to the one thing the prover is for.

quantized_sources.note: The integer originals of every float in the [P] section. The loader prefers these over the floats wherever both exist (CharacterData.cpp:196-228), which is what makes ARCHITECTURE D8 checkable: the engine loads these and the floats exist only for the prover. EVERY ONE OF THEM IS EXACT HERE -- the integers were chosen first and the floats derived from them by dividing by 100, so no conversion in this file rounds and the loader's inexact-quantization warning cannot fire.
quantized_sources.reach_px_note: The two fireballs are ABSENT from this map on purpose. A fireball's reach is a function of distance travelled, so `reach` is authored null and CharacterData.cpp:692-702 leaves reachSub at kNoReach; an entry here would override that null and fabricate range the file declines to claim. MatchBuilder then builds a zero-width box and the move connects with nothing, which is honest and is counted under `move.reach (absent)`.

constants.source: DESIGNED TO MATCH THE KERNEL EXACTLY, which is a thing only an original character can do. health 1000 is ResetMatch's (Simulate.cpp:153-154). walk 512 sub-units/tick is Simulate.cpp:15's hardcoded kWalkSpeed of 2 px/tick, so this character's authored walk_speed of 0.02 reach units quantizes to the number the engine already uses and the `character.walk_speed` loss is nominal rather than real. gravity 64 is kGravity (0.25 px/tick^2) and the jump impulse is kJumpImpulse; neither is exercised, because no move in this file leaves the ground and there is therefore no on_land transition and no A10 to satisfy. The pushbox is MatchBuilder's kDefaultBodyHalfWidthSub/kDefaultBodyHeightSub restated so a harness can supply BuildOptions::body deliberately.

BROKEN_self_chain.caveat: THE DELIBERATE DEFECT. One edge, stand_lp -> stand_lp. See engine.the_bug.

chain.delay_rule: DESIGNED: 2. The chain window is a property of the SOURCE move's animation, not of the target, so every edge out of one normal shares one delay -- which is why the file has one number here and not sixty. 2 rather than 0 because a true cancel on the contact frame is not something this engine can express: StepAttack runs before ResolveHits, so the fastest cancel the kernel has is 1 (Combat.h, Simulate.cpp:90-96), and authoring 0 would make the file claim a frame the game cannot give. ADR-001:434-442 calls the discovery that MUGEN chain cancels are NOT delay 0 'the hardest single finding of the phase' and measures the real range at 2 to 20; 2 is the fast end of that range, chosen so the light tier confirms cleanly.
chain.caveat: lights -> mediums (16 edges) and mediums -> heavies (16). Strictly ascending: there is no L -> L, no M -> M and no H -> anything-lower edge anywhere in this file.

special_cancel.delay_rule: DESIGNED: 2, the same as the chain, for the same reason -- one window per source move. Sources are the four mediums and three of the four heavies; the sweep is excluded because it is an ender.
special_cancel.caveat: The heavy fireball (startup 15) is deliberately NOT a medium's target: 2 + 15 = 17 against 18 frames of hitstun leaves the defender exactly 1 frame, which is a link wearing a cancel's clothes. It is authored only from the heavies, where it has 4-5 frames of margin. Authoring it from the mediums would have produced an edge the prover calls usable and a player cannot confirm, which is the class of mistake this whole project exists to make visible.

super_cancel.delay: 2 out of a normal, 4 out of a special
super_cancel.delay_rule: DESIGNED. Out of a normal the source's own window applies (2). Out of a special it is 4, because a special's cancel window opens later in its animation. THE THREE EDGES OUT OF THE TWO FIREBALLS ARE THE ONE PLACE THIS FILE TOUCHES A KNOWN SOUNDNESS BUG, and it is discharged here rather than deferred -- see engine.fit.known_losses[0].
super_cancel.caveat: Guarded on meter 100 and the super spends 100, so a super cancel is the one edge family in the file that is net-negative on a resource. It can therefore never be part of a loop, which the prover proves rather than assumes: `nonNegative` refuses the transition once meter would go below zero (comboprover.hpp:264-269, :434).

moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.crouch_hk: The sweep is a hard-knockdown ENDER. -11 on hit and it puts the defender on the floor, so there is nothing to cancel into. Authored with cancel_window_ticks [] rather than omitted, which is the case ADR-001:541-545 records as load-bearing.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.special_uppercut_l: A reversal has no follow-up: -18 on hit, and its value is the 8 ticks of invulnerability, not a combo. It has no INCOMING edge either, which is also what keeps a 3-frame startup safe -- ADR-001:512-515 names a 4-frame launcher as 'exactly the shape that fabricates an infinite', and the shape only does that when something can cancel into it or out of it.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.special_uppercut_h: As the light version, -22 on hit.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.super_beam: A super is the end of a combo by definition, and it is the only move in the file that spends a resource.

hit_rules.summary: There are none, and that is the design. No move in this file gates its hit on a predicate over the defender, so move.hit_condition is absent everywhere and engine.hit_condition carries no prose. Kung Fu Girl needs 17 of these because it disables MUGEN's juggle system and runs its own counters instead (ADR-001:255-260); this character has no such rule to lose.
hit_rules.juggle: MUGEN's juggle system has no analogue here and the kernel has none either (Combat.h scopes juggle and proration out with blocking and pushback). The `juggle` resource is declared for the positional contract and spent by nothing.

engine.derivation_legend: Every move's engine.derivation is one string that begins with DESIGNED in capitals, because this character has no source file and there is no .cns line to cite. What follows is the design intent for each number that is not implied by the tier template, and the frame-advantage arithmetic where it decides whether a cancel connects. Schema rule: every [P] field carries a derivation naming a file:line OR saying plainly that it was estimated and by what rule -- there is no third case, so an original character says DESIGNED and states the rule, and assertion A12 is satisfied by construction rather than by citation.

derivation_defaults.frame_advantage: hitstun - (active + recovery), which is the kernel's arithmetic exactly: a move started on tick T frees the attacker on T + startup + active + recovery and a hit on tick T + startup frees the defender on T + startup + hitstun.
derivation_defaults.tier_templates: lights startup 4-5 / hitstun 13-14; mediums startup 6-7 / hitstun 18; heavies startup 8-11 / hitstun 21-22; fireballs startup 13-15; reversals startup 3-4. These are the brief's bands and every move sits inside them.
derivation_defaults.reach: the maximum BODY-TO-BODY GAP at which the move connects, in pixels, which is what CharacterData.h Move::reachSub means and what MatchBuilder.cpp:680-728 builds. It is NOT the sprite's attack box measured from the origin -- that is the discrepancy MatchBuilder flags under `move.reach (provenance)` for the imported characters, and this file avoids it by authoring the quantity the engine actually consumes.
derivation_defaults.pushback: DESIGNED displacement in pixels, scaled to the tier. Unlike the corpus it is not an estimate of an unrecorded quantity, but it is also not exercised: the stage is corner and the kernel moves nobody on hit.
derivation_defaults.damage: hundredths of a damage point, against a health pool of 1000. Lights 20-30, mediums 55-65, heavies 85-100, specials 60-110, super 250.
derivation_defaults.stance_and_blocked_as: Both are per move and both are stated on all eighteen; engine.stance_and_guard carries the rule and each move's engine.stance_and_guard_note carries its own argument.

stance_and_guard.what_this_pass_did: Annotated all eighteen existing moves against schema v3: added none, removed none, and changed no frame number, no delay, no cancel and no resource effect. [P] move.stance replaced with a precise value on all eighteen, [G] move.blocked_as authored on all eighteen, engine.hurtbox_sub on three, engine.airborne_from_tick on NONE. THE FILE'S ONE PURPOSE IS UNAFFECTED AND THAT IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED: the deliberate defect is cancels[0], stand_lp into itself, and it closes on startup + delay < hitstun -- 4 + 2 < 14 -- none of which is a field this pass can reach. See stand_lp's own note.
stance_and_guard.where_the_guard_heights_came_from: OUT OF THIS FILE'S OWN DERIVATION PROSE, MOVE BY MOVE, and not out of the sibling file. Unlike fighter_a.json this character carries an EMPTY engine.tags on every move, so there was no tag to promote; what it has instead is a derivation string per move that argues for its numbers, and four of those strings already state a guard height in English. crouch_lp: `a crouching light trades one frame of stun for hitting low`. crouch_lk: `startup 5 rather than 4 because it hits low`. crouch_mk: `The long low medium`. crouch_hk: `The sweep`. Two moves that PAID FRAME DATA for a property the schema had no field to hold, and two that named it outright. crouch_hp is `the anti-air-ish one` and is therefore a MID. crouch_mp's derivation makes no height claim at all, in a file where every other crouching move does, and is a mid on that silence.
stance_and_guard.the_one_place_the_two_files_disagree: crouch_lp IS A LOW HERE AND A MID IN fighter_a.json, and the disagreement is deliberate rather than an oversight in one of the two. Each file's blocked_as is read out of that file's own evidence: this one's derivation buys the low with a frame of hitstun, while that one's crouch_lp has identical timing to its stand_lp, carries no `low` tag, and is the jab ADR-006 section 2 names in `a sweep and a crouching jab are both crouching and only one is low`. THE TWO FILES ARE SIBLINGS AND NOT COPIES -- this crouch_lp is 4f and that one is 3f, this character has no aerials at all and that one has two, and the notes arrays say plainly that this file is not to be balanced against. Forcing the two to agree would have meant overruling one file's own arithmetic with the other's, which is the opposite of reading the data.
stance_and_guard.the_hurtbox_policy: THREE BOXES, ON THE SAME THREE MOVES AS THE SIBLING FILE and for the same reasons: crouch_mk at 26 px because it ducks, crouch_hk at 20 px because the sweep ducks furthest, crouch_hp at 36 px because it deliberately does NOT and a number says so where a silence would have left the standing 60 px body standing in for a crouch. THE HEIGHTS ARE IDENTICAL ACROSS THE TWO FILES AND THE FORWARD LEANS ARE NOT, which is the rule worth stating: HEIGHT IS A PROPERTY OF THE CHARACTER and LEAN IS A PROPERTY OF THE MOVE, and this character's crouching kicks reach 46 and 50 px here against 72 and 94 px there. The other three crouching moves carry no override and therefore present the default body from engine.constants -- 3328 half-width by 15360 tall -- which OVER-STATES their height, makes them easier to hit, and is the conservative direction as well as the state all eighteen were in before this pass.
stance_and_guard.why_no_move_here_authors_airborne_from_t: BECAUSE THE FILE ALREADY SAYS NO MOVE LEAVES THE GROUND, and it says it as a reason rather than as a shrug: engine.constants.source reads `neither is exercised, because no move in this file leaves the ground and there is therefore no on_land transition and no A10 to satisfy`. The two uppercuts are where a reader will look, and they are the reason to state this rather than leave it to an absence -- fighter_a.json's uppercut DOES author airborne_from_tick 3, derived from an engine.motion keyframe and an on_land transition that exist in that file and not in this one. A tick here would be a number with nothing behind it, in a file whose every value says DESIGNED and states its rule. THE FIELD RECORDS A FACT AND IS NOT A BLANK TO BE FILLED IN.
stance_and_guard.the_census_A16_now_sees: standing 12, crouching 6, air 0, `ground` 0. A16 warns about one line -- air, 0 of 6 -- where before this pass it warned about all three and reported eighteen moves as GROUNDED, STANCE UNSPECIFIED. The standing figure is 12 rather than the convention's 6 because A16 counts BY STANCE and the five specials and the super are standing too; the 6/6/6 standard counts NORMALS, this character has exactly six standing normals, and schema x-load-assertions.A16 records that divergence deliberately. The surviving warning is TRUE AND CORRECT FOR THIS FILE IN PARTICULAR: it has no aerials, on purpose, because its job is one ground loop executed by the kernel and an air move would have been a move the ground truth does not need.
stance_and_guard.cannot_move_a_measured_number: The four fields are read by nothing that decides anything. comboprover.hpp has no stance concept and no blocking; ProverAdapter.cpp's only use of stance is a projection loss count over `!= Stance::Any`, which `standing` and `crouching` satisfy exactly as `ground` did; cse::kernel::MoveDef carries startup, active, recovery, damage, hitstun, hitbox and button and nothing else, so the MatchData hash this file's replay tests compare is byte-identical across the pass; and json_spec.py's _move() reads thirteen named keys and enumerates none. THE ONE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED: ADR-006 section 5 measures model.py:120-121 raising on any stance outside a closed three-value tuple, so this file is unloadable by the unmodified reference implementation until that line is widened to five. It costs this character nothing today -- stage is corner and the corner verdict is the C++ header's -- and it costs the midscreen path everything, because Python is the only midscreen path. ADR-006 section 10 item 7 is the one-line remedy.

engine.cancel_note: 60 edges, 4 families, one delay per source move. The full per-edge table is in `cancels` and every entry names its family; the family carries the delay rule, the certainty and the caveat, so no edge repeats them. `certain` is TRUE on all 60 -- unlike the corpus, where 200 of 247 edges are uncertain because the transcription could not establish the runtime condition gating them, this file has no runtime conditions to be uncertain about.

variants.note: One character, one automaton. No sub-characters, no mode variable and no per-variant gap action, so there is no selector to declare, assertion A11 does not apply, and notes[] carries no union warning. ADR-001 group I is the shape this avoids: the AOF2 thug is a spawner plus four disjoint sub-characters and an INFINITE verdict over the union of its variants can name a route no single sub-character can perform. A one-variant file has no union, so this file's verdict names a route ONE character can perform -- which is what makes it usable as a ground-truth trace at all.

integrity.note: Advisory identifiers, null until Phase 4. The connect handshake hashes the LOADED POD ARRAYS and never this text, so these can never be the desync check.

fit.gate: ARCHITECTURE.md:289 sets the escape-hatch rate at < 20% and ADR-001 measured 1 of 59 under D7's own definition and 23 of 59 under the broader 'needed something the schema cannot say'. This file is 0 of 18 on both readings.
fit.the_measurement_phase_0_could_not_take: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE ZERO. ADR-001's 23-of-59 is the rate at which characters that ALREADY EXISTED needed fields schema v1 did not have. This file's 0-of-18 is the rate at which a character authored knowing the schema needs fields the schema does not have, and the two are different measurements: the second is trivially better and cannot refute or confirm the first. What it DOES establish, and what Phase 0 could not because all three of its characters were MUGEN imports (ADR-001:516-521 names that sampling bias itself), is the other direction -- that the v2 vocabulary is sufficient to author a complete all-rounder from nothing, with a fireball, a reversal, a travelling special and a multi-hit super, without reaching for prose once. Every one of the nine v2 fields that this character's shape calls for is exercised here with real data: engine.motion on the dash punch, engine.hits + hits_projection on the super, engine.projectile on both fireballs, engine.invuln and engine.freeze on the reversals and the super. The four that are NOT exercised are not exercised because the character does not have the shape that needs them, which is stated rather than left to inference: no move leaves the ground (so no on_land transition and no A10), no button selects between two moves by range (so no proximity_variant and no min_reach_sub), no move gates its hit on the defender's state (so no hit_condition), no cancel gates on the opponent's state (so no cancel.engine.condition), and there is one character rather than four sub-characters (so no variants and no A11).
fit.why_no_opponent_predicates: DELIBERATE, and it is the one place where authoring an original character is cheaper than transcribing one. ADR-001 section 4 group G is 'the finding': Kung Fu Girl gates all 17 normals on a juggle predicate and all 26 AOF2 cancels gate on `p2movetype != H`, and neither is evaluable until Phase 5 builds an opponent namespace. Rather than author gates the engine cannot evaluate -- which would make this file describe a character the engine cannot run, and would put the prover in the permissive direction on 60 edges at once -- this character has none. Every gate in the file is a resource guard, which the fragment reads natively.
schema_limits: The prover half of the projectile contact frame is not closable by a schema field. See known_losses[0]; this file is the first in the project to author an outgoing cancel from a projectile, so it discharges the note schema.v2.json leaves for whoever does.
The kernel cannot represent knockdown, so the sweep and the two reversals are ordinary hits to it. Permissive, and inert: none of the three has an outgoing cancel.

move.reach is one horizontal scalar, so the schema authors no vertical extent for an attack at all and a low kick hits a fighter at the top of a jump. Horizontal is the axis the prover reasons on, so this is a kernel-vs-game loss and not a kernel-vs-prover one.
known_losses: PROJECTILE CONTACT FRAME -- the one over-approximation in schema v2 that errs in the DANGEROUS direction, and the only one this file makes LIVE. schema.v2.json x-known-over-approximations.projectile_contact_frame records that it is inert across the whole Phase-0 corpus because Kung Fu Man's two projectiles have zero outgoing cancels. This file's two fireballs have one each (cancels[57] and cancels[58], into the super), so the note applies for the first time. IT IS DISCHARGED, NOT DEFERRED, and the schema says how: 'authoring a projectile move's outgoing cancel delays as if contact were at the minimum plausible range, which over-credits the attacker and flips the direction to the safe one'. Delay 4 is measured from the RELEASE tick, and at point-blank range release and contact coincide, so 4 IS the minimum-range reading. At any greater range the real contact is later and the authored edge is therefore more permissive than reality -- which can invent an infinite and cannot hide one, the direction ADR-001:224-225 calls safe. Bound: 2 edges. Effect on this file's verdict: none, because the verdict is INFINITE on a loop that contains no projectile.

DEFENDER HAS NO STATE -- the prover has no defender at all, so it lets a combo continue past a hit that really ends it. Permissive, safe. Bound: 3 moves whose reaction sets causes_knockdown (crouch_hk, special_uppercut_l, special_uppercut_h). Inert here: none of the three has an outgoing cancel, so there is no combo to continue past them.

ATTACKER DISPLACEMENT -- the kernel does not execute engine.motion, so special_dash_punch connects from where it started. Handled by authoring `reach` as the maximum gap at which the move connects INCLUDING the 54 px it travels first, so the static box reproduces the real total reach exactly. What is lost is where the two fighters END UP, which no field in this schema carries and which the corner model does not read. Bound: 1 move. Not in the loop.

RESOURCES ARE NOT SIMULATED -- Fighter::meter exists and nothing reads or writes it, so the super's guard of 100 is not enforced and its cost of 100 is not paid. Bound: every effect and guard in the file. NOT IN THE LOOP, and this matters: the loop's only resource interaction is a +5 gain, so a kernel that ignores resources and a prover that tracks them agree about it. A loop that depended on spending would not be executable today and this file deliberately does not author one.

HITSTUN DECAY AND DAMAGE SCALING -- the kernel applies neither, so the tenth hit of a combo deals what the first did and stuns for as long. For decay this file agrees with the kernel by construction (kind `none`), so there is nothing to lose. For scaling there is: the prover reports max damage through a 6-entry table the kernel does not apply, so the two disagree about DAMAGE and agree about the VERDICT, which is the half that matters. The loop's KO tick of 202 is computed from the kernel's unscaled 30 per hit and would be later under the authored scaling.

MULTI-HIT -- ResolveHits applies at most one hit per active window, so super_beam lands once for 250 rather than three times for 80/80/90. Damage-only; hitstun is identical on all three records so the [P] projection is exact. Bound: 1 move. Not in the loop.

SCHEMA v3'S FOUR FIELDS ARE DATA AND NOT YET BEHAVIOUR. move.stance is a KernelPermits loss over all 18 moves because the kernel gates starting a move on hitstun and blockstun only -- a `crouching` move is still startable in the air, and making the field precise did not make it enforced. blocked_as is further back still: cse::kernel::Combat.h scopes blocking out entirely (`Fighter::blockstun exists and nothing ever writes it`), so there is nothing yet for a guard height to be checked against. engine.hurtbox_sub gives the DEFENDER a height and the schema still authors no vertical extent for an ATTACK, so until a hitbox has a y-range a shorter crouch is data nothing consumes. Bound: every move in the file. DIRECTION: none -- nothing reads any of the four, which is exactly why this pass cannot have moved the verdict. Authoring the data before the rule is the right order (ADR-006 section 10 item 6); the alternative is a kernel rule with no file able to describe the character it applies to.

per_edge_margins.definition: hitstun remaining on the defender at the tick the follow-up connects, computed the kernel's way: margin = from.hitstun - (max(delay,1) + to.startup). A margin >= 1 is a true combo; a margin of 0 gives the defender exactly one actionable tick; a negative margin is a gap.
per_edge_margins.note: The tightest authored edge in the file has 3 frames of margin and the loop has 8, so the one-frame disagreement between the prover's usability test and the kernel's true-combo test (engine.prover_vs_kernel) is 3 frames away from the nearest edge and cannot decide anything here.

measured.status: NOT MEASURED. This object is where an actual `python -m comboprover analyse` run and an actual kernel trace go, and schema.v2.json requires it to be re-measured and never predicted. Nothing in it may be filled in from the arithmetic in this file.

predicted_not_measured.warning: A PREDICTION, kept in a separate key from `measured` so it cannot be mistaken for one. If a run disagrees with any line below, the run is right and this file is wrong.
predicted_not_measured.verdict: Infinite, corner. The C++ header is corner-only by construction and this file authors stage `corner`, so the two are answering the same question.
predicted_not_measured.loop: [stand_lp], a self-loop of length 1. The witness prefix should be five repetitions of stand_lp, because hitCap = max(settlingIndex + 1, scaling.size()) = max(1, 6) = 6 and the covering test cannot fire until the hit counter saturates.
predicted_not_measured.why_the_witness_is_that_short: cancels[0] is FIRST in the array and stand_lp is FIRST in starters, so outgoing[stand_lp][0] is the self-edge and the depth-first search takes it before anything else. That ordering is deliberate: MatchBuilder.cpp preserves file order and Combat.cpp's FindCancel takes the first matching edge, so the same choice is made in the prover, in the bridge and in the tick.
predicted_not_measured.hasRanking: false, and for the FIRST of ADR-001 gate 3's two reasons rather than the second: every move gains meter, so `spendOnly` is cleared at comboprover.hpp:376-386. It is moot here -- the certificate is only computed for a Terminating verdict.
